title: Wilton Crawley stories
summary: Allen's Barberin story and Russell's anecdote about Wilton Crawley mistaken for an asylum patient, followed by a reel change.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Yeah, I was always going to ask if you have any special, this may not be the place on it on this tape.
We can wait until the tape runs off.
If you have any special angle on Jelly Roll and could write an article.
No, I gave you a thing on that. Jelly Roll's about Wilton Crawley's teeth falling out and all that.
Wait a minute, what was that? No. Oh, yeah. No. You don't remember that? No. You follow those notes away.
I don't have that. You interviewed Paul Barberin, yeah.
Well, I remember all the little white pieces of paper, you know, the official two-lane things.

Oh, no, no, no. I gave you a thing where I interviewed Paul Barberin about Wilton Crawley's teeth falling out. It was a supplement. This doesn't go on the tape. It was really funny. It was a funny story that Paul Barberin told me.
The funniest story on Wilton Crawley is the one that Bob Green interviewed Manzi Campbell. How do you spell Manzi Campbell? With a Z or an S?
I think with a Z. I thought so, too.

Bob thought it was an S. He's gone now. Okay. Well, anyway, Manzi once played a job with Wilton Crawley. Wilton Crawley recorded quite a few jelly songs, about four or six, I forget what they are. And Crawley had his own band, of course, sometimes used some of Lou Russell's band. But they played a date out at some insane asylum, I guess you'd call it, out on Long Island. And some of the guards were responsible from the different buildings to take a certain bunch of the patients, you know, in the little bus. So they had to take them back to the rooms after it was over, the concert. So Wilton Crawley got on one of the buses to go back to the main gate or something. So this one guard, or the bus driver, who was responsible for a certain number, again, checking on his busload to be sure that he had all of his guys going back with him. And he said, I'm going to run across Crawley, going one, two, three, four, and he's ready for five. He sees Crawley sitting there, doesn't remember him. He said, who are you? What's your name?
He said, I'm Wilton Crawley, the world's greatest clarinet player.

And he said, five, six, seven. He's going to go take him and lock him up, too. See, Crawley was about the corniest, if you remember the record, about the corniest player, even worse than Ted Lewis in some ways. He was a contortionist.
He'd get down and roll around on the floor, playing his clarinet and all, too.
Nobody could play. Okay, the third reel is on, Ross.
